forecast.title: Avalanche Canada early season bulletin (all of BC)
forecast.highlights: Avalanches hazard may exist where there is snow. Pack a transceiver, shovel, and probe, and factor avalanches into your trip plan. Daily avalanche forecasts will begin November 25 at 4 PM.

summaries.weather-summary: More details can be found in the Mountain Weather Forecast.

forecast.title: Bow Valley-Highwood Pass-North 40-Spray - KLakes
forecast.highlights: Winter is expected to make a brief appearance over the Thanksgiving weekend. While an avalanche problem is unlikely to develop from this snow, it should cue us all to start thinking of a winter snowpack/avalanche season.

summaries.snowpack-summary: This incoming snow will be our foundational layer. While an immediate avalanche problem is unlikely, the distribution of this snow will be worth noting for future storms.
summaries.weather-summary: More details can be found in the Mountain Weather Forecast.

forecast.title: Avalanche Canada early season bulletin (all of BC)
forecast.highlights:
Fall is here along with cooler temperatures and snow in the high alpine. Pay attention to local snow amounts and watch out for deeper accumulations in alpine lee and gully features.
Regular forecasting will begin November 1st.

summaries.snowpack-summary: The early season snowpack is typically thin and widely variable, presenting deep drifts and areas scoured to the ground. Localized pockets of wind slab are common, meaning it can be easy to step from dry ground into a windslab, so watch carefully for these pockets of snow
summaries.weather-summary:
For current weather conditions, see the telemetry stations on the Avalanche Canada map page.
For weather forecasts, check out Environment Canada's products for Banff, Kootenay and Yoho.
For weather maps, graphics and satellite images check out the Mountain Weather Forecast.
For a technical weather forecast check out SpotWx

forecast.title: Glacier
forecast.highlights:
With the transition to fall, snow has started to accumulate at upper elevations. There have been small avalanches on smooth alpine slopes during recent snowfalls.
Pack a transceiver, probe & shovel, and factor avalanches into your trip if you are travelling in the high country.
Daily avalanche hazard forecasts begin in November.

summaries.snowpack-summary: With cooler fall temps, snow is starting to accumulate in the alpine. Be cautious in areas where the ground is smooth under the snow, and where wind deposits have created localized pockets of deep snow.
summaries.weather-summary:
For current conditions check the telemetry stations by clicking on the weather station icons on the Avalanche Canada map page.
For a weather forecast we recommend Environment Canada's forecast for Roger's Pass
For a weather maps, graphics and satellite images check the Mountain Weather Forecast
For a technical forecast check out SpotWx or Windy
